query: What leave-one-site-out and external validation plan (number of held sites, stratification by scanner/modality) is adequate to demonstrate cross-site generalization for scale-aware models?

response.query: What leave-one-site-out and external validation plan (number of held sites, stratification by scanner/modality) is adequate to demonstrate cross-site generalization for scale-aware models?
response.answer: For scale-aware models, leave-one-site-out cross-validation with at least three held-out sites, stratified by scanner modality, is adequate to demonstrate cross-site generalization. This approach ensures robust evaluation across different data distributions.

results.title: Strategies to Improve the Robustness and Generalizability of Deep ...
results.content: While previous articles have summarized the methods used to increase the robustness and generalizability of machine learning models in general or with a narrow focus on a specific task [21,22,23,24], our review provides an overview of strategies for improving the robustness and generalizability of deep learning models in neuroimaging to achieve a balance between accuracy and multi-modal adaptability for clinical applications. We summarize the previous studies on improving the robustness and generalization ability of deep learning models in neuroimaging segmentation and classification tasks, such as transfer learning, regularization, and adversarial training; we further emphasize the important role of evaluation metrics and uncertainty estimation.
